input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view for training and pipeline runs in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the run comparison capability in the Dashboard: users can
select two or more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and
metrics side by side, including a diff presentation that highlights which
parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. Today parameters and
metrics live only on per-run pages, forcing data scientists to compare runs in
exported spreadsheets; this epic brings that comparison in-platform.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs (training runs and Data Science Pipelines
  runs) from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- A side-by-side comparison view of the selected runs' parameters and metrics.
- A diff presentation mode over the same comparison data that highlights which
  parameters and metrics differ between two selected runs.
- Correct rendering of runs with differing parameter/metric sets (values
  present on one run and absent on another).
- Comparison stays within a single project and cluster, consistent with the
  strategy's out-of-scope statement (no cross-project or cross-cluster
  comparison).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can select two or more runs from the runs list and open a comparison
  showing each run's parameters and metrics side by side.
- Given two selected runs, the comparison highlights which parameters and
  metrics changed between them.
- The comparison correctly renders parameters and metrics for Data Science
  Pipelines runs as well as training runs (validation of the passive Data
  Science Pipelines component — its run data is consumed as-is through
  existing interfaces, with no pipelines-side changes).
- The comparison handles runs whose parameter/metric sets differ without
  errors or silent omission.
- Comparison is offered only for runs within the same project and cluster.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): select two or more runs and view parameters and metrics side by
  side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1, consolidated with HLR-1): run "diff" view highlighting which
  parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs — a presentation
  mode of the same comparison surface, covered by this epic at the higher
  priority rather than split into a separate epic.

# Record the producing run on registered model versions

## Description

This epic delivers run-of-origin lineage in the Model Registry: a registered
model version records the identity of the run (training or pipeline run) that
produced it, and that linkage is exposed through the Model Registry's
interfaces so that a comparison can be opened from a registered model version.
This is the registry-side half of connecting model promotion decisions to the
runs behind them.

## Scope

- Ability to record, at or after registration, which run produced a given
  registered model version, using the Model Registry's existing metadata
  extension points for model versions (the exact mechanism — e.g. custom
  properties versus a dedicated field — is an implementation decision for the
  Model Registry team).
- The run-of-origin linkage is retrievable per model version through the Model
  Registry REST API so that UIs can resolve the producing run.
- Registration flows and existing model versions are not broken: model
  versions without a recorded producing run remain valid.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A registered model version can carry the identity of the run that produced
  it, and that identity is retrievable through the Model Registry REST API for
  a given model version.
- Registering a model version without a producing-run reference still
  succeeds (the linkage is optional metadata, not a required field).
- The linkage round-trips through the API: a client can read back the same
  producing-run identity it recorded for a model version.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them — registry-side recording and exposure of the linkage.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry view in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry entry point to the run comparison
capability: from a registered model version viewed in the Dashboard's Model
Registry section, a user can open a comparison that includes the run that
produced that model version. Model promotion decisions then start from the
registry with side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs, instead of requiring users to go find the runs in the runs list first.

## Description of Dependencies

This epic consumes two capabilities delivered elsewhere in the strategy and
does not re-implement either: the run comparison view (parameters and metrics
side by side, with diff highlighting) and the producing-run linkage recorded
on registered model versions and exposed through the Model Registry REST API.
Both must be available before this epic's work can complete.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry view, a model version that carries a
  producing-run reference offers an action to open a comparison including that
  run.
- The action resolves the producing-run identity through the Model Registry
  and navigates to the existing run comparison view with that run loaded,
  letting the user add further runs to the comparison.
- The entry point is hidden or disabled for model versions that carry no
  producing-run reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From a registered model version in the Dashboard's Model Registry view that
  has a recorded producing run, a user can open a comparison that includes
  that run, rendered by the existing comparison view.
- The user can add one or more further runs to the comparison opened this way,
  for both training runs and pipeline runs.
- Model versions without a producing-run reference show no broken entry point
  (the action is absent or visibly disabled with a clear reason).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry — the
  Dashboard-side entry point over the registry linkage.

# Document the run comparison workflow from the runs list and the registry

## Description

This epic documents the run comparison capability for end users: how to select
and compare training and pipeline runs from the runs list, how to read the
side-by-side and diff presentations, and how to open a comparison from a
registered model version in the Model Registry.

## Scope

Content outline (Red Hat docs content process):

- New documentation topics covering the run comparison workflow:
  - Selecting two or more runs from the runs list and opening the comparison.
  - Reading the side-by-side parameters/metrics view and the diff
    presentation highlighting what changed between two runs.
  - Opening a comparison from a registered model version in the Model
    Registry, including the prerequisite that the model version carries a
    producing-run reference.
- Screenshots of the comparison view, diff presentation, and registry entry
  point.
- Cross-links between the runs-list documentation, the Model Registry
    documentation, and the new comparison topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the
  runs list: multi-run selection, the side-by-side view, and the diff
  presentation.
- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the
  Model Registry: opening a comparison from a registered model version and its
  producing run.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  capability (reviewed by or with the implementing engineers) before
  publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.
